theme: I believe I shall look upon the goodness of the LORD
readingInstruction: Read Psalm 27. It is a psalm of David that begins with confidence and moves into a plea. Notice the one thing David asks for, and how the psalm ends with an exhortation to wait.
settingTheScene: Psalm 27 is a psalm of David, probably from a time of danger from enemies. It has two parts: verses 1 to 6 are a song of trust, and verses 7 to 14 are a prayer for help. It fits our reading in 1 Thessalonians, where believers faced persecution, and in the Prison Epistles, where Paul writes from chains. The psalm teaches us that confidence in God and honest prayer belong together.
observation: “The LORD is my light and my salvation; whom shall I fear?” (v. 1).
“Though an army encamp against me, my heart shall not fear” (v. 3).
“One thing have I asked of the LORD, that will I seek after: that I may dwell in the house of the LORD all the days of my life” (v. 4).
“To gaze upon the beauty of the LORD and to inquire in his temple” (v. 4).
“For he will hide me in his shelter in the day of trouble” (v. 5).
“You have said, Seek my face. My heart says to you, Your face, LORD, do I seek” (v. 8).
“For my father and my mother have forsaken me, but the LORD will take me in” (v. 10).
“I believe that I shall look upon the goodness of the LORD in the land of the living!” (v. 13).
interpretation:
David begins with three titles for God: light, salvation, and stronghold. “The LORD is my light and my salvation; whom shall I fear? The LORD is the stronghold of my life; of whom shall I be afraid?” Light dispels darkness, salvation rescues, stronghold protects. When evildoers assail him to eat up his flesh, they stumble and fall. “Though an army encamp against me, my heart shall not fear; though war arise against me, yet I will be confident.” The confidence is not in himself but in the LORD.

Then the heart of the psalm: “One thing have I asked of the LORD, that will I seek after: that I may dwell in the house of the LORD all the days of my life, to gaze upon the beauty of the LORD and to inquire in his temple.” Of all that he could ask, David asks for one thing: God’s presence. This is the great desire of the believer. In the temple, he gazes on the beauty of the LORD. The dwelling place of God is the source of safety: “For he will hide me in his shelter in the day of trouble; he will conceal me under the cover of his tent; he will lift me high upon a rock.” The result is joy: “I will offer in his tent sacrifices with shouts of joy; I will sing and make melody to the LORD.”

The second half is a prayer. “Hear, O LORD, when I cry aloud; be gracious to me and answer me!” David recalls God’s call: “You have said, Seek my face. My heart says to you, Your face, LORD, do I seek. Hide not your face from me.” The invitation to seek God’s face is God’s own. We pray because he invited us. Even if his parents forsake him, which is a deep fear, “the LORD will take me in.” God is a better father than any earthly one. He asks to be taught God’s way and led on a level path, because of his enemies, who breathe violence.

The psalm ends with a statement of faith and an exhortation. “I believe that I shall look upon the goodness of the LORD in the land of the living!” The believer expects to see the goodness of God now, not only in the age to come. And then David turns to us: “Wait for the LORD; be strong, and let your heart take courage; wait for the LORD!” Waiting is the posture of trust. In Christ, our greatest desire is met. He is the true temple, where God dwells with us. He is the light of the world. The beauty of the LORD is seen “in the face of Jesus Christ” (2 Corinthians 4:6).
connection: Psalm 84:1-4 also speaks of longing for God’s dwelling. Psalm 63:1-3 and 42:1-2 speak of thirst for God. John 1:14 and 8:12 present Christ as the dwelling and the light. 2 Corinthians 4:6 speaks of seeing God’s glory in Christ’s face. Isaiah 49:15 speaks of God’s care exceeding a mother’s. Isaiah 40:31 promises renewal to those who wait. Romans 8:31-39 assures us that nothing can separate us from God’s love. Hebrews 10:19-22 invites us into God’s presence. Revelation 21:22-23 pictures God as the temple and Lamb as the light.
application:
Ask the question: if I could ask for one thing from God, what would it be? Let it be to know him.

Take five minutes to gaze on the beauty of the LORD: read a passage about Christ and meditate on his character.

Wait for the LORD today in a specific matter, and ask him to strengthen your heart.
prayerPrompts: Tell God what you fear, and say, “The LORD is my light and salvation.”
Ask him for the one thing: to dwell with him and see his beauty.
Wait for him and take courage.
